title: Watchlist of Record
description: The single handoff artifact of the trading day. Written once by the desk at the open, immutable for the session. The monitor reads this and nothing else — it has no license to discover new names. Anything interesting the monitor sees off-list is an input to TOMORROW's flow analysis, not today's trade.

session_date.description: Trading date in the desk timezone.

frozen.description: Once true the name list may not be extended intraday. Levels may be revised by the desk with an appended revision entry; names may not be added.

revisions.description: Append-only. Any intraday change to a level or trigger lands here with a reason. The original value is never overwritten in place.

sources.description: Provenance. Which upstream artifacts this watchlist was built from.

brief.description: Path to the market brief artifact, or null if the brief agent failed.

flow.description: Path to the flow candidates artifact, or null if the flow agent failed.

degraded.description: True when any upstream stage failed. A degraded watchlist is still tradeable but the client is told which leg is missing.

regime.description: The one-paragraph read of the tape that everything on the list is conditioned on. If this breaks, the whole list is suspect — that is what regime_invalidation is for.

regime_invalidation.description: The observable event that would mean this read is wrong. Must be checkable by the monitor.

capital.description: Risk envelope for the session. The desk owns these; the monitor enforces them.

names.description: Ranked. Cap is deliberate: the monitor's cost and the client's attention both scale with this number. An empty list is a legitimate and sometimes correct output — say so plainly rather than manufacturing names.

bias.description: watch_only means: interesting, not yet actionable. It still gets monitored.

thesis.description: One sentence a client would understand. If it takes a paragraph, the thesis is not clear enough to trade.

evidence.description: Why this name is here. Each field is null when that line of evidence is absent — never a zero, never an empty string standing in for 'we did not look'.

flow.description: The UW observation that surfaced this name.

repeat_days.description: How many consecutive sessions this flow has printed. Repeat is the highest-value signal in this dataset and the one most often missed by a single-day scan.

macro.description: How the brief's regime read bears on this name, or null if it does not.

positioning.description: GEX / max pain / OI structure context.

note.description: Whether we are buying or selling premium into this, and why that is the right side.

levels.description: Prices, all on the underlying unless noted. reference_price is what everything else was computed against — without it the levels cannot be audited later.

invalidation.description: Below/above this the thesis is wrong. Not a stop-loss on the option — a statement about the underlying.

structure_hint.description: Suggested expression, e.g. 'debit call spread 2-3 DTE'. A hint, never an order. The desk sizes and the human decides.

triggers.description: THE critical field. This is what the monitor watches. The monitor evaluates these mechanically and does not invent its own — that is what keeps it cheap, fast and non-hallucinating.

id.description: Stable dedup key, e.g. 'NVDA:price_cross:182.50'. The monitor keys its alert state on this, so it must not change intraday.

urgency.description: info: log only. action: an opportunity, batchable into the next cycle summary. risk: interrupt the client now. Only positions and regime breaks should ever be 'risk'.

condition.description: Machine-checkable. The monitor must be able to evaluate this from a UW response without judgement.

cooldown_minutes.description: After firing, suppress this id for this many minutes. Without this the monitor re-alerts the same level every cycle for four hours and the client mutes the desk by 10am.

max_fires.description: Hard cap per session. null means unlimited, which should be rare.

note.description: What this trigger means, in client language, for use in the alert text.
